Toast.SmtcHint.Body: The player can hear the audio but gets no title or cover. Turn on the system media control (SMTC) switch in NetEase Cloud Music → Settings and the title, cover and control buttons will work. It also works with that switch off — the bars and the record still react to the music.
Sandbox.Title: Started in a restricted environment
Sandbox.Body:
This process is running with low integrity (sandboxed), so these features will not work:

· Tray icon (the shell refuses the registration)
· Config saving (%APPDATA% writes are denied — widgets will disappear after a restart)
· Audio session detection (CoreAudio interfaces are unavailable)

Close it and start DeskOrder.exe from File Explorer (not through a sandbox / host process).

Settings.Renderer.Wallpaper.Hint: When on, liquid glass draws its own backdrop from the current wallpaper instead of asking DWM, so the blur-radius slider becomes real pixels (DWM blur is fixed-strength on Windows 11, which is why the slider used to do nothing). The backdrop is sampled at 1:1 screen resolution and laid out per monitor, so each glass window keeps its own bitmap (about 29 MB per radius on a full desktop, up to 6 cached). When off, the original DWM path is used and the look matches older versions exactly: colour, opacity and luminosity still apply, but materials and blur radius take no part in rendering.
Settings.Renderer.Resample.Hint: Click after changing the wallpaper or when its content has moved on — the new sample is pushed to every glass window immediately. Glass windows step aside briefly (about 0.1s); other windows (including this one) only step aside for the instant of the capture, which is imperceptible.

LiquidGlass.Hint: Blur=0 disables | Luminosity 100%=original | Preset sets base tint | With wallpaper-sampled rendering the blur radius is real pixels (backdrop samples the wallpaper); the material picks the backdrop recipe and grain
